proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(d<T\), put \(I_d=\{1,\ldots,d\}\cup B_d\), and write
\(h_d=(w,a,d,x_{1:d})\).  By the definition of \(g_d\), it is the
joint mass of \((W,A,X,D=d)\).  Exact recovery on \(Z=1\), followed by
the audit-randomization assumption, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\Pr_P\!\left(W=w,A=a,D=d,X_{1:d}=x_{1:d},
                 Z=1,X_{B_d}=x_{B_d}\right)\\
&\quad=\sum_{x_r:\,r\notin I_d}
 g_d(w,a,x_{1:T})
 \Pr_P\!\left(Z=1\mid W=w,A=a,X=x_{1:T},D=d\right)\\
&\quad=e_d(h_d)\sum_{x_r:\,r\notin I_d}g_d(w,a,x_{1:T})
 =e_d(h_d)M_d(w,a,x_{I_d}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The factor \(e_d(h_d)\) may be taken outside the sum because it depends
only on the displayed routine history.  Audit positivity permits division
by this known factor, so every cell of \(M_d\) is determined by the law of
\(O\).  This remains true when \(B_d=\varnothing\): the event \(Z=1\)
then identifies the routine cell multiplied by \(e_d(h_d)\).

For the unaudited cell, the same calculation and marginalization over the
bundle give
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\Pr_P\!\left(W=w,A=a,D=d,X_{1:d}=x_{1:d},Z=0\right)\\
&\qquad=\{1-e_d(h_d)\}
   \sum_{x_{B_d}}M_d(w,a,x_{1:d},x_{B_d}).
\end{aligned}
\]
At \(d=T\), all substantive coordinates are routine coordinates and
\(Z=0\) deterministically, so the corresponding observed cell has mass
\(g_T(w,a,x_{1:T})=M_T(w,a,x_{1:T})\).  These displayed formulas also
prove the converse: from the tables and the always-observed \((W,A)\)
law, multiply by \(e_d(h_d)\) for audited cells, multiply the indicated
marginal by \(1-e_d(h_d)\) for unaudited cells, and use \(M_T\) for
complete cells.  The structural cells just listed partition the alphabet
of \(O\), so they determine its entire law.  Thus both transformations are
finite and linear once the known design probabilities are fixed.

Fix \(d<T\) and let \(b_d=\min\{T,d+2\}\).  If \(s\le d\), every index
in \(S_s\) is at most \(s+1\le d+1\), while every index in
\(S_{d+1}\) is at most \(d+2\).  Hence all response factors occurring
in \(g_d\) depend only on \((w,a,x_{1:b_d})\).  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
u_d(w,a,x_{1:b_d})
={}&p_W(w)p_A(a\mid w)K_1(x_1\mid w,a)
       \prod_{r=2}^{b_d}K_r(x_r\mid w,a,x_{r-1})\\
&\times\prod_{s=1}^{d}q_s(w,a,x_{S_s})
       \{1-q_{d+1}(w,a,x_{S_{d+1}})\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The substantive-positivity and hazard-positivity assumptions imply that
\(u_d\) is strictly positive.  The substantive Markov factorization, the
local-hazard assumption, and conditional independence of the response
noises give, with an empty product interpreted as one,
\[
g_d(w,a,x_{1:T})
=u_d(w,a,x_{1:b_d})
  \prod_{r=b_d+1}^{T}K_r(x_r\mid w,a,x_{r-1}).
\]

Now take \(b_d\le k<\ell\le T\).  Sum the last display over
\(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1}\).  The resulting joint mass of
\((W,A,X_k,X_{k+1:T},D=d)\) has the form
\[
c_{d,k}(w,a,x_k)
\prod_{r=k+1}^{T}K_r(x_r\mid w,a,x_{r-1}),
\]
where \(c_{d,k}(w,a,x_k)>0\); positivity follows because it is a finite
sum of positive terms.  Each \(K_r\) is a normalized conditional kernel,
so summing the suffix product over \(x_{k+1:T}\) gives one.  Division by
the positive conditioning mass therefore yields
\[
\Pr_P(X_{k+1:T}=x_{k+1:T}\mid
      X_k=x_k,W=w,A=a,D=d)
=\prod_{r=k+1}^{T}K_r(x_r\mid w,a,x_{r-1}).
\]
Finally, marginalizing all suffix coordinates except \(x_\ell\) gives
\[
\Pr_P(X_\ell=x_\ell\mid X_k=x_k,W=w,A=a,D=d)
=\sum_{x_{k+1:\ell-1}}
  \prod_{r=k+1}^{\ell}K_r(x_r\mid w,a,x_{r-1}),
\]
which is precisely the composed kernel \(K_{k+1}\cdots K_\ell\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: An explicit finite interval-block state space, an exhaustive list of recovery and obstruction rules, a termination proof, and a positive countermodel-gluing theorem for arbitrary \(T\) and every local-parent interaction remain to be constructed.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen certificate handle is a research program rather than a definition of \(\mathsf A\): it specifies neither the finite states nor a rule deciding every residual state. Positive scaling can identify a target on singular strata, while interacting parents can preserve all overlapping audit margins and still change the endpoint. The supplied four-visit witness rules out the natural path-coverage closure, and no argument supplied in the core proves that the listed normalization, transport, curvature, and rank branches exhaust all response fibers.
open_obligations.attempted: I verified pattern-table equivalence and the local Markov-tail factorization, then tested the proposed closure architecture against the single-informative-hazard construction, complementary positive-scaling logic, alphabet-sensitive rank branching, and the stated four-visit parent-interaction counterexample. These establish sound individual moves but do not yield a residual-state dichotomy or a gluing induction.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The two foundational reductions are complete: randomized auditing is
exactly equivalent to observing the pattern tables, and every dropout
subdensity has the stated two-step boundary followed by an unselected
Markov suffix.  In addition, the single-informative-hazard subclass has a
complete arbitrary-horizon recovery-or-positive-witness alternative, as
proved in the partial result for that proposition.  These results certify
pattern marginalization, risk-set addition, legal positive normalization,
and Markov-tail transport.  They do not establish that the proposed list
of operations is exhaustive when several local hazards interact.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The theorem awaits the exhaustive recovery-or-witness alternative posed by the open-ended question.
open_obligations.obstruction: Neither \(\mathsf A\) nor its branch invariant has been defined, so recovery soundness and obstruction completeness cannot be used as proved premises. Treating the certificate handle itself as that theorem would assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted: I reduced both directions of the claimed equivalence to the two outputs required from the missing alternative and checked that audit-table equivalence supplies the necessary passage from observed laws to pattern tables.
open_obligations.partial_result:
If the requested exhaustive alternative were proved for a specified
procedure \(\mathsf A\), the equivalence theorem would follow immediately
and without an additional regularity premise.  Indeed, on a recovery
branch, equality of the laws of \(O\) implies equality of every \(M_d\) by
the audit-table proposition, and hence
\[
Q(P)=\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}((M_d(P))_{d=0}^T)
    =\mathsf{Rec}_{T,S,B}((M_d(P'))_{d=0}^T)=Q(P').
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1\).  On an obstruction branch, the
returned pair satisfies equal observed laws and unequal target vectors,
which is exactly a counterexample to graphwise identification.  This
argument also shows that vector identification, null allowed-arrow
effects, and deficient ranks require no separate logical step once the
alternative itself is available.  What is missing is the premise of this
reduction: the exhaustive alternative has not been constructed or proved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Monotonicity and enumeration for the frozen certificate criterion await the equality of that criterion with graphwise identification.
open_obligations.obstruction: Audit marginalization proves monotonicity of graphwise identification, but the frozen statement is about \(\mathsf C\), whose behavior is not fixed until the missing procedure and completeness theorem are supplied.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved the larger-bundle marginalization argument and counted the admissible bundle inclusions exactly; I then isolated the sole unavailable substitution \(\mathsf C=\operatorname{GID}\).
open_obligations.partial_result:
Monotonicity is already provable at the graphwise-identification level.
Suppose \(B\le B'\) and two laws have the same observed law under \(B'\).
By audit-table equivalence their \(B'\)-pattern tables agree.  Marginalizing
each table over the coordinates in \(B'_d\setminus B_d\) produces the
corresponding \(B\)-pattern table, so those tables agree as well.  A second
application of audit-table equivalence gives equality of the observed laws
under \(B\).  Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B')=1.
\]
Once \(\mathsf C=\operatorname{GID}\) is established, the same implication
holds for \(\mathsf C\).  There are
\[
2^{\sum_{d=0}^{T-1}(T-d)}=2^{T(T+1)/2}
\]
designs, because each of the \(T(T+1)/2\) admissible pairs \((d,j)\) is
included or excluded independently.  Filtering all successes by strict
coordinatewise inclusion then equals the defining set \(\mathfrak F\).
Thus only the unavailable identification equivalence prevents closure of
the frozen criterion-level statement.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Only the translation of the complete single-hazard graphwise characterization from \(\operatorname{GID}\) to the undefined certificate value \(\mathsf C\) remains open.
open_obligations.obstruction: The causal identification boundary and positive countermodel are provable directly, but the statement is phrased in terms of \(\mathsf C\), so its final equivalence depends on the unresolved constructive-completeness theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: I derived an explicit recovery in both possible pre-hazard dropout regimes and built a positive arbitrary-alphabet countermodel by common survivor subdensity scaling, including a strictly positive Markov tail that transports the hidden marginal difference to the endpoint.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The following graphwise version of the claimed reduction is fully proved.
Condition throughout on a positive cell \((W=w,A=a)\).  Suppose that the
only continuation probability allowed to vary with the trajectory is
\(q_k(w,a,x_j)\), where
\(j\in\{k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\).  Then the endpoint law is
graphwise identified if and only if
\[
\tag{SH}
\text{there are }d<k\text{ and }\ell\ge j\text{ such that }\ell\in B_d.
\]

For sufficiency, assume (SH) and fix such \(d,\ell\).  Complete cases
identify the positive tail kernel
\[
L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z)
=\Pr(X_T=x\mid X_\ell=z,W=w,A=a,D=T),
\]
with the identity kernel used when \(\ell=T\).  Every response factor
after visit \(k\) is constant conditional on \((w,a)\), and the sole
nonconstant factor depends on \(X_j\), where \(j\le\ell\).  The
first-order Markov factorization therefore gives
\[
L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z)
=\Pr(X_T=x\mid X_\ell=z,W=w,A=a).
\tag{1}
\]
All denominators in this equality are positive by substantive and hazard
positivity.

If \(d\le k-2\), the event \(D=d\) only involves response probabilities
that are constant conditional on \((w,a)\).  It is therefore independent
of the substantive trajectory, and the audited table identifies
\[
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)
=\Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=d)
=\Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a).
\tag{2}
\]
If \(d=k-1\), the risk event \(D\ge k-1\) is independent of the
trajectory.  Put
\[
\rho_{w,a}
=\frac{\Pr(D\ge k\mid W=w,A=a)}
        {\Pr(D\ge k-1\mid W=w,A=a)}.
\]
The denominator is positive, and \(0<\rho_{w,a}<1\), by hazard
positivity.  Later response probabilities are constant, so the
distribution of \(X_\ell\) conditional on \(D\ge k\) equals its
distribution conditional on \(D=T\).  Partitioning the risk set according
to continuation at visit \(k\) yields the identified mixture
\[
\begin{aligned}
\pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)
={}&(1-\rho_{w,a})
 \Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=k-1)\\
&+\rho_{w,a}
 \Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a,D=T)\\
=&\Pr(X_\ell=z\mid W=w,A=a).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The first conditional distribution in (3) is obtained from the audited
\(d=k-1\) table, and the second is routine in complete cases.  Equations
(1)--(3) give the evaluable reconstruction
\[
Q_a(x)=\sum_w p_W(w)\sum_{z\in\mathcal X_\ell}
       \pi_{\ell,w,a}(z)L_{\ell,w,a}(x\mid z).
\tag{4}
\]

For necessity, suppose (SH) fails.  It is enough to construct the pair in
one treatment stratum and keep all other treatment strata, the positive
law of \(W\), and the positive treatment mechanism fixed.  Choose two
distinct strictly positive mass functions \(\mu,\mu'\) on
\(\mathcal X_j\).  Choose a positive vector \(c\) satisfying
\[
0<c(z)<\min\{\mu(z),\mu'(z)\}
\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal X_j.
\tag{5}
\]
Make \(X_1,\ldots,X_{j-1}\) mutually independent with common positive
laws in the two models.  In the first model let the conditional law of
\(X_j\), ignoring its allowed predecessor, be \(\mu\); in the second use
\(\mu'\).  Define the sole informative hazards by
\[
q_k(z)=\frac{c(z)}{\mu(z)},
\qquad
q'_k(z)=\frac{c(z)}{\mu'(z)}.
\tag{6}
\]
Condition (5) makes both hazards strictly between zero and one.  Take all
other hazards to be the same constants in \((0,1)\).

Choose common positive downstream transition kernels so that the two
endpoint marginals differ.  Such kernels exist for every specified finite
alphabet.  Explicitly, for each \(r\ge j\) choose a nonconstant function
\(h_r\) with \(\lvert h_r\rvert\le1\) and mean zero under a strictly
positive mass function \(\nu_r\).  Choose \(\mu,\mu'\) so that their
expectations of \(h_j\) differ, and, for \(r>j\), set
\[
K_r(y\mid z)=\nu_r(y)
 \{1+\lambda_r h_{r-1}(z)h_r(y)\},
\qquad 0<\lambda_r<1.
\tag{7}
\]
These are normalized strictly positive kernels.  Moreover,
\[
\mathbb E\{h_r(X_r)\mid X_{r-1}=z\}
=\lambda_r h_{r-1}(z)
  \sum_y\nu_r(y)h_r(y)^2.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus the difference of the endpoint expectations of \(h_T\) is the
nonzero difference at visit \(j\), multiplied by strictly positive
factors.  If \(j=T\), the initial difference itself suffices.  Hence at
least one endpoint cell probability differs.

It remains to verify observational equivalence.  For every \(d\ge k\),
the full dropout subdensity is identical pointwise in the two models,
because the only changed product at visit \(j\) satisfies
\[
\mu(z)q_k(z)=c(z)=\mu'(z)q'_k(z).
\tag{9}
\]
For \(d\le k-2\), failure of (SH) implies that every coordinate in
\(I_d\) is strictly smaller than \(j\).  Those coordinates have the same
joint law in both models, and summing the changed suffix gives one, so
\(M_d=M'_d\).  For \(d=k-1\), the same observed-coordinate statement
holds, while marginalizing the failure factor at visit \(k\) gives in
both models
\[
\sum_z\{\mu(z)-c(z)\}
=1-\sum_zc(z)
=\sum_z\{\mu'(z)-c(z)\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Therefore all pattern tables agree.  Audit-table equivalence gives equal
laws of \(O\), whereas (8) gives unequal endpoint intervention laws.
Every substantive and response entry is strictly positive.  Independent
uniform disturbances realize the specified finite kernels, so the pair is
a legal causally sufficient Markovian SCM pair.  This proves necessity.

Consequently the inclusion-minimal graphwise-sufficient designs are
exactly those having one inclusion \(B_d=\{\ell\}\), all other bundles
empty, with \(d<k\le j\le\ell\).  Translating this proved characterization
from \(\operatorname{GID}\) to the frozen symbol \(\mathsf C\) requires
the still-open constructive-completeness theorem and is the only missing
step for the frozen proposition.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The statistical limit follows on any regular branch once the population reconstruction is known to equal \(Q\); that equality is unavailable because constructive completeness is open.
open_obligations.obstruction: Continuous differentiability alone yields a limit centered at \(F(o)\). Identifying that center with the causal target requires the missing recovery theorem and cannot be inserted by definition.
open_obligations.attempted: I carried out the finite-multinomial continuity and delta-method reduction, including the fixed known-audit-probability linear composition, and isolated \(F(o)=Q\) as the only identification-dependent step.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on the unproved equality \(F(o)=Q\), the asymptotic argument
is complete.  The finite multinomial law gives
\[
\widehat o_n\longrightarrow o\quad\text{in probability},
\qquad
\sqrt n(\widehat o_n-o)
\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top\right).
\]
Continuity of \(F\) gives consistency.  Continuous differentiability at
\(o\) and the multivariate delta method give
\[
\sqrt n\{F(\widehat o_n)-F(o)\}
\Rightarrow
N\!\left(0,
DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top\right).
\]
If the local extension is only defined on a neighborhood of \(o\), define
the estimator arbitrarily off that neighborhood; the probability of this
modification tends to zero.  Known-probability inverse-weighted pattern
tables are a fixed finite linear transform of the observed-cell histogram,
so composition with that transform gives the corresponding conclusion.
The unresolved identification theorem is needed solely to justify
\(F(o)=Q\) from \(\mathsf C=1\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq 1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), a design \(B\), and a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\).  Enumerate the \(m\) structural cells of \(\mathcal O\) by \(r=1,\ldots,m\), and write
\[
Y_{i,r}=\mathbf 1\{O_i=r\},\qquad
o_r=\Pr_P(O_i=r),\qquad
\widehat o_{n,r}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nY_{i,r}.
\]
By \(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\), for each fixed \(r\), the variables \(Y_{1,r},\ldots,Y_{n,r}\) are independent Bernoulli variables with common mean \(o_r\).

We first derive the concentration inequality needed below.  If \(Y\) is Bernoulli with mean \(\mu\), put
\[
h(\lambda)=\log\mathbb E\!\left[\exp\{\lambda(Y-\mu)\}\right].
\]
Exponential tilting preserves the two-point support \(\{0,1\}\).  Hence, if \(\nu_\lambda\) is the tilted mean, direct differentiation gives
\[
h(0)=h'(0)=0,
\qquad
h''(\lambda)=\nu_\lambda(1-\nu_\lambda)\leq\frac14.
\]
Taylor's theorem therefore yields \(h(\lambda)\leq\lambda^2/8\) for every real \(\lambda\).  Independence then gives, for \(t>0\) and \(\lambda>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_P\!\left\{\widehat o_{n,r}-o_r\geq t\right\}
&=\Pr_P\!\left\{e^{\lambda\sum_{i=1}^n(Y_{i,r}-o_r)}\geq e^{\lambda nt}\right\}\\
&\leq e^{-\lambda nt}\prod_{i=1}^n
  \mathbb E_P e^{\lambda(Y_{i,r}-o_r)}\\
&\leq \exp\!\left(-\lambda nt+\frac{n\lambda^2}{8}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The first inequality follows directly from
\(\mathbb E[V]\geq c\Pr(V\geq c)\) for a nonnegative random variable \(V\).  Taking \(\lambda=4t\) gives the upper-tail bound \(e^{-2nt^2}\).  Applying the same calculation to \(-(Y_{i,r}-o_r)\) gives
\[
\Pr_P\!\left\{|\widehat o_{n,r}-o_r|>t\right\}
\leq 2e^{-2nt^2}.
\]
Finiteness of \(\mathcal O\), supplied by \(\text{ass:finite-alphabets}\), permits a union bound over its \(m\) cells.  With \(\varepsilon_n=\sqrt{\log(2m/\alpha)/(2n)}\), the event
\[
E_P=\left\{\|\widehat o_n-o\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon_n\right\}
\]
satisfies
\[
\Pr_P(E_P^c)
\leq\sum_{r=1}^m2e^{-2n\varepsilon_n^2}
=2m\exp\{-\log(2m/\alpha)\}
=\alpha.
\]
By the definition of \(o\), \(o=\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P)\).  On \(E_P\), the law \(P\) itself therefore satisfies both constraints in the braces defining \(\mathcal C_n\): it belongs to \(\mathcal P_{T,S,B,e}\) by hypothesis, and
\[
\|\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(P)-\widehat o_n\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon_n.
\]
Consequently \(Q(P)\) belongs to the set inside the closure in \(\text{def:projected-confidence-set}\), and hence belongs to \(\mathcal C_n\).  Thus
\[
\Pr_P\{Q(P)\in\mathcal C_n\}
\geq\Pr_P(E_P)
\geq1-\alpha.
\]
This argument uses neither identification nor differentiability and therefore also covers singular and nonidentified strata.

It remains to verify the claimed finite polynomial-optimization representation.  Let \(\theta\) collect the finitely many entries of \(p_W\), \(p_A\), \((K_t)_{t=1}^T\), and \((q_t)_{t=1}^T\).  By \(\text{def:scm-class}\), its parameter set \(\Theta^\circ\) is specified by finitely many stochastic-table normalization equalities together with the strict polynomial inequalities
\[
p_W(w)>0,\quad p_A(a\mid w)>0,\quad K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1})>0,
\quad q_t(w,a,x_{S_t})>0,
\quad 1-q_t(w,a,x_{S_t})>0,
\]
where the irrelevant \(x_0\) argument is omitted at \(t=1\).  All index sets are finite by \(\text{ass:finite-alphabets}\).

For a complete trajectory define
\[
f_\theta(w,a,x_{1:T})
=p_W(w)p_A(a\mid w)K_1(x_1\mid w,a)
 \prod_{t=2}^T K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1})
\]
and, with an empty product equal to one,
\[
\rho_{d,\theta}(w,a,x_{1:T})=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\left\{\prod_{t=1}^{d}q_t(w,a,x_{S_t})\right\}
\{1-q_{d+1}(w,a,x_{S_{d+1}})\},&0\leq d<T,\\[6pt]
\displaystyle\prod_{t=1}^{T}q_t(w,a,x_{S_t}),&d=T.
\end{cases}
\]
The substantive factorization in \(\text{ass:substantive-markov}\), the local-hazard formula in \(\text{ass:local-hazards}\), conditional independence in \(\text{ass:response-noise-independence}\), and the recursion \(R_t=R_{t-1}C_t\) imply
\[
\Pr_\theta(W=w,A=a,X=x_{1:T},D=d)
=f_\theta(w,a,x_{1:T})\rho_{d,\theta}(w,a,x_{1:T}).
\]
For \(d<T\), set \(I_{d,0}=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and \(I_{d,1}=\{1,\ldots,d\}\cup B_d\), and set
\[
c_{d,1}(h_d)=e_d(h_d),
\qquad c_{d,0}(h_d)=1-e_d(h_d).
\]
For an observed cell with \(D=d<T\), audit value \(Z=z\), and displayed substantive values \(v\), \(\text{ass:audit-randomization}\) gives the exact coordinate formula
\[
[\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(\theta)]_{d,z,v}
=c_{d,z}(h_d)
\sum_{x_{1:T}:\,x_{I_{d,z}}=v}
f_\theta(w,a,x_{1:T})\rho_{d,\theta}(w,a,x_{1:T}).
\]
For \(d=T\), the analogous formula has \(z=0\), coefficient one, and no unobserved substantive coordinate.  The audit probabilities are known constants at the displayed histories.  Each coordinate of \(\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(\theta)\) is therefore a finite sum of finite products of entries of \(\theta\), and hence is a polynomial.  Similarly, the causal target supplied by intervention on \(A\) is
\[
Q_{a,x}(\theta)=
\sum_{w,x_1,\ldots,x_{T-1}}
p_W(w)K_1(x_1\mid w,a)
\prod_{t=2}^T K_t(x_t\mid w,a,x_{t-1}),
\qquad x_T=x,
\]
which is also a polynomial in \(\theta\).  Notice that this formula is the causal intervention functional, not a definition in terms of the observed law; its equality to \(P(X_T=x\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\) follows from the Markovian substantive SCM and the intervention replacing the structural equation for \(A\).

Define the finite-dimensional feasible set of primitive tables
\[
\mathcal F_n^\circ=
\left\{\theta\in\Theta^\circ:
-\varepsilon_n\leq
[\Phi_{T,S,B,e}(\theta)]_r-\widehat o_{n,r}
\leq\varepsilon_n\ \text{for every }r=1,\ldots,m
\right\}.
\]
Thus, for every coordinate \((a,x)\), the two programs
\[
L_{a,x}=\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal F_n^\circ}Q_{a,x}(\theta),
\qquad
U_{a,x}=\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal F_n^\circ}Q_{a,x}(\theta)
\]
have finitely many variables and finitely many polynomial equality and inequality constraints, and polynomial objectives.  They are therefore finite constrained polynomial optimization problems.
If a formulation using only weak polynomial inequalities is desired, each strict constraint \(g(\theta)>0\) can be represented exactly by adjoining a variable \(s_g\) and imposing \(g(\theta)\geq0\), \(s_g\geq0\), and \(g(\theta)s_g-1=0\).  Thus strict positivity introduces no non-polynomial constraint.
By \(\text{def:projected-confidence-set}\),
\[
\mathcal C_n=\operatorname{cl}\{Q(\theta):\theta\in\mathcal F_n^\circ\}.
\]
The ambient finite product \(\prod_{a\in\mathcal A}\Delta(\mathcal X_T)\) is compact.  Hence, whenever \(\mathcal F_n^\circ\) is nonempty, \(\mathcal C_n\) is nonempty and compact, its \((a,x)\)-coordinate extrema are attained, and continuity of coordinate projection gives
\[
\min_{q\in\mathcal C_n}q_{a,x}=L_{a,x},
\qquad
\max_{q\in\mathcal C_n}q_{a,x}=U_{a,x}.
\]
If \(\mathcal F_n^\circ\) is empty, the same finite programs simply report infeasibility.  On the coverage event \(E_P\), it is nonempty because it contains the true primitive table \(\theta(P)\).  This proves both assertions.
